name: Area-Impulse
description: A mechanic, often found in wargames, where play proceeds in a series of impulses or sub-phases. During each impulse, players might activate a limited number of units or groups of units within a specific area or across the board. The impulse system continues until all players pass consecutively or a certain number of impulses are completed, often signifying the end of a larger turn or round. This creates a back-and-forth flow and requires careful decisions about activation order and tempo.

parameters.name: Number of Activations per Impulse
parameters.description: How many units or groups can a player activate when it's their turn within an impulse (e.g., one unit, one stack, units in one area).

parameters.name: Impulse Ending Condition
parameters.description: What causes the series of impulses to end for the current round/turn (e.g., all players pass, fixed number of impulses, specific event).

parameters.name: Passing Rules
parameters.description: Can players pass their turn in an impulse? Does passing prevent further action in the larger round, or only in the current series of impulses?
parameters.default_value: Passing means no more activations in the current impulse series

parameters.name: Initiative System
parameters.description: How is turn order determined within each impulse, or for the start of a new impulse series?
parameters.default_value: Alternating turns, fixed start player per round

examples_in_games.game_name: Storm Over Arnhem / Storm Over Stalingrad (Series)
examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Classic examples of the area-impulse system. Players activate formations in impulses until both pass.

notes_on_combination_modification: Area-impulse systems allow for a granular yet manageable control over large numbers of units by breaking down a turn into smaller decision points. It emphasizes the importance of timing and reacting to opponent's moves. The complexity can vary greatly, from simple 'I go, you go' impulses to intricate systems with varied activation capabilities.
